title: NavVis raised €73.7M to build the spatial data layer that factories need before they can deploy AI
excerpt: Munich-based NavVis raised €73.7M Series D to scale its spatial twin platform. Over 1B sqm of industrial space scanned. BMW, VW, Toyota, Siemens, BASF are customers.
content_html:
TL;DR

NavVis raised €73.7M Series D led by The Jordan Company. Spatial twin platform has scanned 1B+ sqm. 1,500+ customers including BMW, VW, Toyota, Siemens. Expanding in US market. Partners with Nvidia, SAP, Autodesk.

NavVis, a Munich-based spatial twin platform, raised €73.7 million ($85 million) in a Series D round led by US private equity firm The Jordan Company. Existing investors Yttrium, KOZO KEIKAKU ENGINEERING, and Cipio Partners also participated. The company, a 2013 spin-off from the Technical University of Munich, builds photorealistic digital replicas of factories, plants, and buildings using wearable laser scanning systems that it says work 10 times faster than traditional survey methods.

The numbers are substantial. More than a billion square metres of industrial space have been scanned onto the NavVis platform, and over 150,000 users in engineering, maintenance, and construction teams use the data daily. The customer list reads like a manufacturing index: BMW, Volkswagen, Toyota, Mercedes-Benz, ExxonMobil, BASF, Henkel, Bosch, and Siemens. The company has partnerships with Nvidia, SAP, and Autodesk, and operates in more than 50 countries with over 1,500 customers.

The investment will fund next-generation capture hardware, a deeper AI intelligence layer, and an open platform for what NavVis calls the “physical AI ecosystem.” CTO Georg Schroth framed the problem: industrial teams have always planned against drawings nobody fully trusts. NavVis replaces those drawings with a continuously updated spatial record that serves as the system of truth for every team, tool, and AI system. Digital twins have been expanding from urban planning to industrial operations, and NavVis sits at the factory end of that spectrum, where the stakes are highest and the data requirements most demanding.

The company is accelerating its US expansion, where it says it has been scaling fastest in recent years. CEO Felix Reinshagen described the mission as keeping physical and digital reality synchronised for the world’s most valuable assets. Customers use NavVis data to reduce downtime on automotive assembly lines, accelerate data centre construction, shorten refinery maintenance shutdowns, plan robotics rollouts, and train industrial foundation models. The spatial data layer is increasingly the prerequisite for industrial AI, and NavVis is positioning itself as the company that builds it.

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

NavVis 筹集了由 Jordan Company 领投的 7370 万欧元 D 轮融资。 空间双胞胎平台已扫描1B+平方米。 1,500 多家客户，包括宝马、大众、丰田、西门子。 拓展美国市场。 与 Nvidia、SAP、Autodesk 合作。

总部位于慕尼黑的空间双胞胎平台 NavVis 在由美国私募股权公司 The Jordan Company 领投的 D 轮融资中筹集了 7370 万欧元（8500 万美元）。 现有投资者 Yttrium、KOZO KEIKAKU ENGINEERING 和 Cipio Partners 也参与其中。 该公司于 2013 年从慕尼黑工业大学分拆出来，利用可穿戴激光扫描系统构建工厂、厂房和建筑物的逼真数字复制品，据称该系统的工作速度比传统测量方法快 10 倍。

这个数字是巨大的。 超过 10 亿平方米的工业空间已被扫描到 NavVis 平台上，工程、维护和施工团队中超过 150,000 名用户每天使用这些数据。 客户名单读起来就像制造业指数：宝马、大众、丰田、梅赛德斯-奔驰、埃克森美孚、巴斯夫、汉高、博世和西门子。 该公司与 Nvidia、SAP 和 Autodesk 建立了合作伙伴关系，在 50 多个国家/地区开展业务，拥有 1,500 多个客户。

该投资将为下一代捕获硬件、更深层次的人工智能智能层以及 NavVis 所谓的“物理人工智能生态系统”的开放平台提供资金。 首席技术官 Georg Schroth 提出了这个问题：工业团队总是根据没人完全信任的图纸进行计划。 NavVis 用不断更新的空间记录取代了这些绘图，作为每个团队、工具和人工智能系统的真实系统。 数字孪生已经从城市规划扩展到工业运营，而 NavVis 处于该范围的工厂端，其中风险最高，数据要求也最高。

该公司正在加速其在美国的扩张，据称其在美国的扩张速度是近年来最快的。 首席执行官菲利克斯·雷因沙根 (Felix Reinshagen) 将其使命描述为保持物理和数字现实同步，以保护世界上最有价值的资产。 客户使用 NavVis 数据来减少汽车装配线的停机时间、加速数据中心建设、缩短炼油厂维护停机时间、规划机器人部署以及训练工业基础模型。 空间数据层日益成为工业人工智能的先决条件，而 NavVis 将自己定位为构建该层的公司。
